confirmed.title: Blank/whitespace name fallback is index-based and mints a duplicate "Player N" colliding with an existing row
repro: Fresh page (clear localStorage) -> open /index.html -> New game (4 default rows Player 1-4)
Remove the first row (roster is now Player 2, Player 3, Player 4)
Clear the second row's name (the "Player 3" row) and type only spaces, then Tab
Tap Skip photo on every row
confirmed.expected: The blanked row gets a placeholder no other player is using (setup's own Add player already avoids minting a duplicate "Player N")
confirmed.actual: Start-time fallback is index-based (Player i+1), so the game starts with two players both named "Player 2"; the pass screen reads "PASS THE PHONE TO Player 2 - then Player 2" and standings show two identical rows distinguishable only by seat color; state confirms players = ["Player 2","Player 2","Player 4"]
sources: roster:Blank (whitespace) name's start-time fallback mints a duplicate "Player 2" that collides with an existing row
confirmed.rationale: Single report, no dedupe. Not by-design per the brief. Reporter proposed S4, but S4 is polish/subtle inconsistency; the consequence here is the pass screen — whose entire job is naming who gets the phone — giving an ambiguous instruction every turn for the whole game, plus indistinguishable standings rows. That matches S3's "misleading copy / janky-but-recoverable flow" (recoverable because seat colors and player memory disambiguate, and no rule outcome or data is wrong, so it is not S2/S1). Trigger requires a deliberate whitespace-only name after removing a row, but the rubric scores impact, and the impact persists all game.

v1.reason: Reproduced first try on the live site via UI-only Playwright (script + 4 screenshots in scratch/qa/round-6/verify-roster-blank-name-duplicate-placeholder-1/): fresh visitor -> New game -> remove row 1 (roster Player 2/3/4) -> blank second row to spaces -> skip photos -> Shuffle & start. __timeline.state players = ["Player 2","Player 2","Player 4"]; pass screen reads "PASS THE PHONE TO Player 2 then Player 2" and standings show two identical Player 2 rows differing only by seat color — exactly as claimed. Mechanism confirmed in code: ui.js:1800 start-time fallback is index-based while freePlaceholderName (ui.js:860-867) dedupes only Add player, so this is an inconsistency the code's own comments condemn, not by-design (brief's list doesn't cover it). S3 stands per rubric: misleading copy / janky-but-recoverable (game-long ambiguous pass instruction, but no broken feature, no wrong rule outcome, colors disambiguate) — above S4 polish, below S2.

confirmed.title: Pass-screen hero name has no max-width/wrap clamp: an unbroken 16-char name clips off both edges at every phone width and drags the hint line off-screen
repro: New game -> name Player 1 'WWWWWWWWWWWWWWWW' (16 chars, input maxlength allows it), tap Skip photo on every row
Look at the pass-the-phone screen at any phone width (320, 375, 393, or 428 px wide)
confirmed.expected: The big hero name shrinks or wraps to fit the screen, the way the win screen's .win__name was explicitly retuned in rounds 4 and 5 for this exact 16-char wide-glyph worst case
confirmed.actual: #pass-player-name renders 492-615 px wide and is clipped off both screen edges at 320/375/393/428 (e.g. left:-86 right:406 at 320w), and because it blows out the centered .pass__stack, the hint line 'Tap when only they can see the screen - the song starts right away' is also clipped at both edges at every phone width; two-word 16-char names wrap and are unaffected. Root cause: .pass__name (app.css ~line 1535) uses clamp(32px, 10vw, 40px) with no max-width/overflow-wrap
sources: responsive:Pass-screen hero clips an unbroken 16-char name off both edges at every phone width, dragging the instruction copy off-screen with it
confirmed.rationale: Single report, no dedupe. Not by-design. Reporter's S3 is what the rubric supports: S2 requires broken layout that hides CONTROLS at a common size, and the reporter's own boundary check shows the whole hero remains a working tap-to-continue target and the name stays legible in the standings list — so this is an overflow/visual defect (clipped display text plus a clipped static instruction line), squarely S3. Strong evidence: rect measurements across four widths, a wrapping two-word control case isolating the unbroken-string trigger, and a named root cause (the win-screen clamp never applied to .pass__name).

v1.reason: Reproduced the exact repro on the live site in real Chrome. With a 16-char unbroken name (WWWWWWWWWWWWWWWW, allowed by the input's maxlength=16), #pass-player-name measured 492.1px wide at 320w (left -86.1, right 406.1 — matching the reporter's -86/406), 576.7px at 375w, 604.4px at 393w, and 615.2px at 428w, clipped off both viewport edges at every width; the .pass__hint line also measured off both edges at all four widths (constant 436.6px inside the blown-out .pass__stack). A two-word 16-char control name wrapped to 254px and did not clip, isolating the unbroken-string trigger. Root cause confirmed in public/music/app.css:1535 — .pass__name uses clamp(32px, 10vw, 40px) with computed overflow-wrap:normal and max-width:none, while .win__name (app.css:2408) got the round-4/5 retune plus overflow-wrap with a comment calling both-edge clipping never acceptable, so this is not by-design. Severity holds at S3, not S2: tapping #btn-pass-continue at 393w still advanced to the play screen, no page-level horizontal scroll, and the name remains legible (ellipsized) in the standings list — no control is hidden, making this rubric-S3 overflow/visual defect. Evidence in scratch/qa/round-6/verify-pass-screen-long-name-clips-both-edges-1/.

(3) manifest.json 200 well-formed (standalone, portrait, 3 icons — svg any+maskable and 180x180 apple-touch — all fetch 200 with correct content-types); head icons 200; service worker registers, activates, controls; reload second visit + fresh second tab both work. (4) Resume: mid-turn save (seed 91, named players, card drawn, gap selected) → reload → home shows "Resume game / Turn 1 — Maren, Otto, Priya, Quinn" → resume lands back on the play screen with turn, active player, drawn card, all four timelines/tokens/names, deck length (1180), mode/target byte-identical (pre/post JSON saved), and even the selected gap ("Placing before 1977") restored. (5) Menu sheet from every screen that has one (pass #btn-menu-pass, play #btn-menu, reveal #btn-menu-reveal — the round-5 fix): every row exercised (Scoreboard round-trips back to the originating screen from both pass and reveal; How to play round-trips; Home keeps the game saved; End game two-tap arm with label change); aria-expanded syncs true/false across all three buttons on open/close from every screen; focus moves into the sheet on open, 8 Tab stops all stay in-sheet, Esc closes and returns focus to the exact opener (btn-menu-pass and btn-menu-reveal respectively).
